claims.text: A tailored post-cold-deformation annealing treatment can induce fine coherent nanoprecipitates in a eutectic high-entropy alloy's lamellar colonies.
The induced precipitates are analogous to δ-lamellae and γ″ particles.
The target eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies containing numerous internal boundaries prone to room-temperature tensile microcrack initiation.
Sufficient prior deformation introduces a high dislocation density needed for the treatment.
The treatment produces fine coherent nanoprecipitates along or within lamellar-colony interfaces.
Fine coherent nanoprecipitates pin dislocations and enhance work hardening.
The same nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission across lamellar boundaries.
Facilitated dislocation transmission relieves local stress concentrations at lamellar boundaries.
Relieving boundary stress concentrations reduces or delays microcrack initiation.
The treatment will simultaneously improve room-temperature tensile strength and ductility relative to the unmodified eutectic structure.
The ultimate tensile strength improvement may be roughly 1 GPa.
Related thermomechanically processed refractory high-entropy alloys can attain high strength together with appreciable ambient-temperature tensile ductility.
Eutectic high-entropy alloys lacking the targeted treatment exhibit brittle behavior, early internal-boundary microcracking, and limited tensile ductility.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration can coarsen the precipitates or cause loss of coherency.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency negates the proposed strength–ductility benefit.
The exact annealing parameters and quantitative property improvements are alloy-specific and require empirical optimization.
The proposed experiment compares identically prepared control and post-deformation-annealed sample sets using room-temperature tensile tests and microstructural characterization.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility, or failure to observe coherent nanoprecipitates, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
